Watcom shadow-pointer walk (two-step form) — `pCVar9` is advanced into scratch `pCVar8`, then rebound via a later `pCVar9 = pCVar8;`. Functionally identical to the single-line self-update; replace `pCVar9->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer and drop both the advance line and the rebind.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar9` self-updates via pointer arithmetic on an inner array field reached through a chained field path; the array decays to a pointer and `+ CONST` adds `CONST * sizeof(element)` bytes, matching the outer array stride. Replace `pCVar9->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

'pCVar6[1].base.create_event + 8' walks 1 x sizeof(CWeapon) (0x594) + offsetof(base.create_event) (0x78) + 0x8 = 0x614, which is exactly offsetof(CFirestaff, flames). Ghidra had no CFirestaff type here and reached the field by index arithmetic; write it as ((CFirestaff *)pCVar6)->flames (§de-pun/§12). Ambiguous: CMelee::thrust_hit_character_sound[88] also has a field there — confirm the real class from the .asm before rewriting.
